_notes: Phase 1 placeholder set — 7 real (non-AI-generated) fridge photos, free-licensed via the Unsplash API
(the same source app.py's /api/dish-image already uses). Hand-verified by a human looking at each photo,
not scraped/synthetic labels. These are Western/mixed fridges, not the Indian-fridge context the app's
prompt is specifically tuned for (dabbas, plastic-bagged produce, door condiments) — acceptable for
validating the harness mechanics, but the score on this set should NOT be treated as the app's real-world
accuracy number. Swap in real (ideally Indian-fridge) photos under photos/ and matching entries here
once available; nothing else about the harness needs to change.
Per photo: `certain` = confidently, unambiguously identifiable by a human looking at the photo — this is
what recall/precision are actually scored against. `partial` = genuinely ambiguous/occluded/unreadable even
to a human (unclear jar contents, food in an opaque bag, blurry/out-of-focus) — NOT scored strictly (an
item here isn't a miss if absent, isn't a hallucination if reported), but the eval script reports whether
the model found them anyway, since partially-recovering these is a genuine bonus signal. `distractors` =
visible non-food or blacklist-category items a correct scan should NOT report — reporting one is a
hallucination event even though it's 'real' in the photo, since it isn't a cookable ingredient.
Names are written the way the app's own prompt asks the model to answer: singular, generic English, no
brand names — so matching is apples-to-apples.

photos.description: Cluttered, multi-shelf home fridge, decent lighting, many packaged items with readable labels
French fridge, dense small-text label reading test (cheese/dairy brand names), a shellfish dish
Clean, well-lit produce drawer — the 'should be easy' baseline case
Glass jars with visible contents + two produce drawers
Meal-prep containers with only partially visible contents (the 'opaque container' test) + varied fresh produce
Poor/colored lighting stress test — magenta ambient light
Warm/yellow lighting stress test, genuinely messy everyday fridge, includes a ground-meat edge case
